decisions_proposed.title: Redefine the size target per profile
decisions_proposed.decision: 16 MB is not reachable without dropping utls/REALITY, the QUIC stack and mihomo's HTTP fork. Proposed targets (stripped, arm64): Ultra <=24 MB, Lightweight <=31 MB, Performance = current lean 37 MB; MIPS +15%. Report xz size (flash) next to it: Ultra ~7-8 MB.
decisions_proposed.confidence: medium (Ultra figure is an estimate from the trial build + per-module weights)

decisions_proposed.title: Per-protocol build tags via stub files
decisions_proposed.decision: Follow the existing tailscale/zerotier/easytier stub pattern: each protocol file gets //go:build !no_<proto> and a stub returning 'disabled at build time'; switches stay untouched (rebase-friendly). Patches needed beyond stubs: vless xhttp-h3, DoH3/DoQ, QUIC sniffer (for no_quic), shadowsocks plugins restls/kcptun, geodata protobuf (no_geosite_dat).

decisions_proposed.title: Memory target defined as private memory
decisions_proposed.decision: Measure and report RssAnon + kernel memory attributable to the core (pipes, sockets) as the RAM metric; report RssFile separately. Require the binary on flash (/usr/bin), never /tmp.

decisions_proposed.title: First memory patches
decisions_proposed.decision: (a) provider load concurrency 1-2 on low-memory profiles (one build-tagged file); (b) .mrs reader without per-element binary.Read allocations; (c) cap splice pipe size (e.g. 64-256 KiB) on low-memory profiles - needs a sing patch or a replace; (d) default GOMEMLIMIT/GOGC from /proc/meminfo when env is unset. Each measured on BPI-R4 before/after.

decisions_proposed.title: DIRECT fast path = pre-interception bypass of NEW connections
decisions_proposed.decision: No hand-back of terminated connections (impossible). The core marks a connection bypass-eligible only if its verdict is IP-determinable: the matched rule and every earlier rule that could match differently depend only on (dst IP, dst port, network[, src IP]); earlier non-determinable rules are allowed only if their outbound is the same DIRECT. Fake-IP connections and sniffed-host decisions are never eligible. Eligible keys go to an nft timeout set checked before interception; invalidation = flush set + conntrack delete by ct mark on every rule/config change and on core start/stop. Glue (clashwrt) owns the nft table; the core only emits verdicts (flow agent option C) behind a build tag.

decisions_proposed.title: eBPF scope
decisions_proposed.decision: Reject XDP, TC-BPF, sk_lookup, cgroup hooks for the core. sockmap verdict redirect for terminated DIRECT TCP: optional experiment only (Performance profile, build tag, raw-syscall loader preferred over cilium/ebpf +1.6 MB), adopted only if BPI-R4 shows a clear CPU win over splice. Fallback = splice (today's path).

decisions_proposed.title: Rust components
decisions_proposed.decision: Not for stages II-X: cgo breaks the pure-Go static cross-build and needs musl toolchains; Rust MIPS targets are tier 3; crypto on MIPS/ARMv7 is no faster; Go runtime overhead stays. meow-rs is used only as an external comparison baseline.

decisions_proposed.title: CPU levers before code
decisions_proposed.decision: Profile defaults and docs: tproxy/redirect or TUN system stack instead of mips/gvisor userspace stacks; ChaCha20-Poly1305 or VLESS-vision on MIPS/ARMv7 (no AES asm); tun.gso where the kernel allows; PGO only with a real MIPS/ARMv7 profile (4pda volunteers).

decisions_proposed.title: Toolchain
decisions_proposed.decision: Build with the newest stable Go (1.27.x) unless a benchmark shows a regression vs upstream's 1.26; record Go version in every BENCHMARKS row. CGO_ENABLED=0, non-PIE, -trimpath -s -w -buildid=.

agent_opportunities.name: Prune features by build tags
agent_opportunities.description: Introduce build tags to exclude tailscale, easytier, zerotier, mieru, wazero, reedsolomon, gopacket, pprof, rarely used protocols; keep pclntab proportional.
agent_opportunities.expected_benefit: Binary from ~56 MB toward the 16 MB goal (tailscale+wazero+easytier+... are tens of MB of the 56); lower init allocations and idle RSS floor.
risks: touching upstream-merged code increases merge conflicts

agent_opportunities.name: Serialize / bound rule-provider loading on 64-bit
agent_opportunities.description: Replace the arch-based concurrentCount (MaxInt on arm64/amd64) with a small constant (1-2) for lightweight profiles, preferably as a tag-selected file mirroring concurrent_load_*.go.
agent_opportunities.expected_benefit: Removes the largest probable contributor to the ~42 MB startup spike; cost is slightly slower startup. Measurable via gctrace on BPI-R4.
risks: Startup time grows with many/large providers
Hypothesis not yet verified by measurement

agent_opportunities.name: Ensure Go splice path is actually used for DIRECT relay
agent_opportunities.description: Audit the fork's tunnel relay (statistic wrappers, buffered conns) so that for DIRECT TCP the bare *net.TCPConn pair reaches io.Copy and Go's splice(2) kicks in; add a tracker that counts bytes via TCP_INFO instead of wrapping Read/Write.
agent_opportunities.expected_benefit: Less userspace copy CPU on DIRECT TCP with zero kernel feature dependency (high on weak CPUs, hypothesis).
risks: Splice is skipped if any wrapper type appears

agent_opportunities.name: Prefer nft set + flowtable for classified DIRECT bypass (not eBPF)
agent_opportunities.description: Keep classified-flow bypass in nftables sets with timeouts and rely on flowtable; eBPF map approach is not recommended.
agent_opportunities.expected_benefit: Safe, fw4-compatible, auto-cleanup, no kmod-sched-bpf.
risks: Set element churn costs CPU on weak routers

agent_opportunities.name: Static CIDR bypass set (extend what clashwrt does) as an optional core module
agent_opportunities.description: Move/mirror clashwrt's static interval-set bypass (RU CIDR, private ranges) into the core so mihomo can emit it itself, loading it with metacubex/nftables, without per-connection logic.
agent_opportunities.expected_benefit: Large share of DIRECT traffic (RU/LAN) offloadable with zero per-connection overhead and no safety risk from shared CDN IPs, because the key is the policy-defining IP range, not a domain verdict.
risks: Requires nft/fw4 present; must auto-disable on non-OpenWrt hosts

agent_opportunities.name: Conntrack-mark based invalidation helper
agent_opportunities.description: Mark bypass-accepted flows with a dedicated ct mark and implement a Go ctnetlink delete-by-mark routine run on config reload/crash recovery.
agent_opportunities.expected_benefit: Deterministic flush of offloaded DIRECT flows without per-flow tuple tracking; required for any dynamic mode.
risks: Needs ctnetlink access (CAP_NET_ADMIN) and a netlink library for conntrack (vishvananda/netlink or hand-rolled)
Brief connection resets for long flows after a reload

agent_opportunities.name: Capability detection with auto-disable
agent_opportunities.description: At start-up probe nft, flowtable presence, NSS/ECM or vendor offload, SQM instance, and refuse to activate dynamic fast path when policy cannot be guaranteed.
agent_opportunities.expected_benefit: Prevents silent unsafe configurations; matches the project requirement of auto-disable.
risks: Detection heuristics for vendor stacks are fragile

agent_opportunities.name: Runtime memory profile from config/wizard
agent_opportunities.description: Add a runtime section (gogc, memory-limit, gomaxprocs) applied at startup and on reload via debug.SetGCPercent/SetMemoryLimit, with presets chosen by detected RAM (64/128/256/512 MB).
agent_opportunities.expected_benefit: Cuts peak RSS (est. 15-30% on small heaps; unmeasured) and prevents unbounded growth; zero binary cost.
risks: limit below live set causes GC thrash (50% CPU limiter)

agent_opportunities.name: Smaller initial read buffer for idle connections
agent_opportunities.description: In the relay path, avoid pinning 16-32 KiB per blocked Read for non-ReadWaiter conns: start with 2-4 KiB or use wait-then-read where possible; grow adaptively.
agent_opportunities.expected_benefit: Saves ~16-32 KB per idle connection (e.g. 16-32 MB at 1000 conns), large for 128 MB devices.

agent_opportunities.name: Per-arch crypto defaults and cipher advice
agent_opportunities.description: On ARMv7/MIPS prefer ChaCha20-Poly1305 or no-crypto-over-TLS paths; on arm64 with AES ext prefer AES-GCM; expose in wizard based on /proc/cpuinfo features.
agent_opportunities.expected_benefit: Potentially large CPU/throughput difference on MIPS/ARMv7 where no asm exists (unmeasured).
risks: benchmarks needed on real MT7621/IPQ40xx/ath79 devices

agent_opportunities.name: Batch reads in .mrs readers and zstd decoder tuning
agent_opportunities.description: Read leaves/labelBitmap/ranges with a single io.ReadFull into a byte slice and decode with binary.BigEndian.Uint64, avoiding millions of per-element binary.Read heap allocations; create the zstd decoder with concurrency 1 and a bounded window.
agent_opportunities.expected_benefit: Lower transient allocation and GC pressure during provider load; fewer goroutines.
risks: Touches upstream files (rebase conflicts), mitigate with small isolated helper functions

agent_opportunities.name: Per-protocol stub tags (no_quic, no_ssh, no_openvpn, no_mieru, no_sudoku, no_kcp, no_wireguard, no_restls, no_jls)
agent_opportunities.description: Follow the tailscale/zerotier/easytier stub pattern: add `//go:build !no_X` to the real adapter/listener file and a stub file defining the Option struct and a New* that returns an error. parser.go/listener/parse.go stay untouched.
agent_opportunities.expected_benefit: Binary size reduction (quic family, mieru+protobuf, jls, utls consumers are the top candidates); exact savings must be measured by builds.
risks: Option structs duplicated in stubs drift on rebase
Shared transports (vless/vmess/trojan) import quic-go/utls so cannot be removed without touching them

agent_opportunities.name: Make the fake-IP cache size configurable or larger when RAM allows
agent_opportunities.description: Size is hardcoded to 1000 entries (config.go ~1545); for routers with many clients, evictions cause 'fake DNS record missing' and failed long-lived connections. Raise via config or tie to fake-ip-ttl.
agent_opportunities.expected_benefit: Stability (priority 1) under many domains; RAM cost negligible (tens of bytes per entry).

agent_opportunities.name: Dynamic destination-IP bypass set fed from tunnel decisions
agent_opportunities.description: Add a hook after match() in tunnel.go (resolveMetadata result = DIRECT, rule chain purely IP/port based) that adds the real DstIP to an nft set maintained by mihomo, modelled on sing-tun's interval-set code and metacubex/nftables; ties into route-exclude-address-set machinery.
agent_opportunities.expected_benefit: DIRECT flows skip the userspace relay and can be flow-offloaded (kernel conntrack/flowtable).
risks: Shared CDN IPs: an IP learned for a DIRECT domain may also serve a PROXY domain -> leak
Fake-IP clears DstIP; need the real IP from the dialer
Must invalidate on rule/provider/config change and fake-ip flush
First packets (conntrack) before the set entry exists

agent_opportunities.name: Keep sing splice path healthy for DIRECT + REDIRECT/TPROXY inbound
agent_opportunities.description: Already present; add regression test/CI check that DIRECT CONNECT tunnel still hits splice (gdb/strace counters as in F003) and prefer redirect/tproxy or system stack over mipstack/gvisor for router profiles so inbound conns are real sockets.
agent_opportunities.expected_benefit: Hypothesis: highest gain per complexity; zero-copy relay for direct/unwrapped flows, lower CPU and no pool buffers.
risks: Pipe 1 MiB cap RAM on many bulk flows

agent_opportunities.name: Build tag with_low_memory + GC tuning (GOGC/GOMEMLIMIT) per profile
agent_opportunities.description: Smaller 16/8 KiB buffers and a memory limit in Ultra/Lightweight profiles.
agent_opportunities.expected_benefit: Hypothesis: several MB RSS saved under load; small CPU increase from GC.
risks: More GC cycles on weak CPUs
throughput drop with 16 KiB chunks on non-splice paths

agent_opportunities.name: Prefer transparent redirect/tproxy over TUN on routers
agent_opportunities.description: Make redirect/tproxy the documented fast mode so inbound conns are kernel sockets and avoid userspace TCP stack and double packet crossing.
agent_opportunities.expected_benefit: Hypothesis: largest throughput and RAM gain vs mipstack/gvisor.
risks: Feature gap for non-TCP/UDP protocols (ICMP), UDP needs TPROXY

agent_opportunities.name: Hand classified DIRECT TCP flows to kernel (nftables flow offload / set bypass)
agent_opportunities.description: After rule match -> DIRECT, install the flow into a kernel fast path (see project key question); mihomo's own splice remains the safe fallback.
agent_opportunities.expected_benefit: Hypothesis: removes proxy CPU for bulk direct flows entirely; best gain for DIRECT-heavy home traffic.

agent_opportunities.name: nft-set + flowtable fast path for classified DIRECT
agent_opportunities.description: Put IPs classified DIRECT by mihomo into an nft set (timeouts) matched early in a prerouting chain in clashwrt's table to skip tproxy/mark; the connection then stays on the forward path where fw4's flowtable ft offloads it.
agent_opportunities.expected_benefit: Direct traffic runs at software-offload speed (no local socket, no userspace copy), lowest CPU on mt7621/ipq40xx
risks: Offloaded flows are not re-evaluated after policy change: need flush of flowtable/conntrack on config change
DNS-based classification races (IP shared by proxied and direct domains)
fw4 flow_offloading must be on and kmod-nft-offload present

agent_opportunities.name: Runtime capability probe
agent_opportunities.description: At start probe nft table support (sets with timeout, flowtable, tproxy), /sys/kernel/btf, kmod presence and auto-disable fast path if any is missing.
agent_opportunities.expected_benefit: Safe degradation on stripped images
risks: Probing by loading kmods may side-effect firewall state

agent_opportunities.name: Do not adopt Rust; spend effort on Go-side tuning
agent_opportunities.description: Keep the pure-Go CGO_ENABLED=0 matrix and use build tags, GOGC/GOMEMLIMIT, kernel fast path for DIRECT.
agent_opportunities.expected_benefit: Keeps MIPS support and rebase-ability; most RAM/CPU wins are available without Rust.
risks: Go runtime floor of several MB remains

agent_opportunities.name: Re-index the fork after each optimization stage
agent_opportunities.description: Run xerj autoindex on the fork (prefix mlw-fork, --fresh) after every merged stage, so impact analysis and regression search see current code.
agent_opportunities.expected_benefit: Fast definition/usage lookup across fork + deps during refactors (build-tag splits touch many files).
risks: stale hits if forgotten (search reports index_stale hint)

agent_opportunities.name: Capability probe for BPF features at startup
agent_opportunities.description: Probe BPF_MAP_CREATE(SockHash)+BPF_PROG_LOAD(SkSKB) and log availability; expose in diagnostics only, no behavior change.
agent_opportunities.expected_benefit: Gives data to decide whether any eBPF path is viable across the five targets.

agent_opportunities.name: Raw-syscall minimal BPF loader instead of cilium/ebpf
agent_opportunities.description: Hand-written loader on x/sys/unix for just map create/update, prog load, prog attach, with pre-assembled instructions.
agent_opportunities.expected_benefit: Saves ~1-2 MB binary (measured standalone delta of cilium/ebpf) and avoids btf code.

agent_opportunities.name: On-device benchmark: splice vs sockmap vs buffered copy
agent_opportunities.description: Prototype a small C/Go test sockmap relay and measure on MT7621 (MIPS32), MT7981/7986 (arm64), IPQ40xx (ARMv7).
agent_opportunities.expected_benefit: Turns hypotheses F008/F023 into data to make the module decision.

agent_opportunities.name: Dynamic exact-key bypass with timeout (saddr . daddr . dport)
agent_opportunities.description: On successful DIRECT dial where the rule is IP/port based or the IP is policy-uniform, add an element with a short timeout via a batched Go worker; remove on DNS remap or config reload.
agent_opportunities.expected_benefit: Subsequent connections (parallel browser connections, keep-alive reconnects) are routed in kernel and offloaded; frees mihomo from bulk transfers (downloads, video).

agent_opportunities.name: Idle FreeOSMemory / scavenger tuning
agent_opportunities.description: After connection count drops below a threshold or on a long idle timer, call debug.FreeOSMemory (currently only on debug API) and keep madvdontneed=1.
agent_opportunities.expected_benefit: Lower observed RSS after bursts (returning freed spans and shrunk stacks).
risks: one full GC pause/CPU burst per call

agent_opportunities.name: Use with_low_memory for small-RAM profiles and measure the UDP-8K limit
agent_opportunities.description: Enable the tag for Ultra Lightweight/Lightweight and validate UDP datagrams >8 KiB (TUN MTU up to 9000) are not truncated.
agent_opportunities.expected_benefit: Halves relay/UDP buffer sizes; fewer bytes in flight per connection.
risks: UDP truncation if read buffers < datagram

agent_opportunities.name: Statistics and connection tracking off switch
agent_opportunities.description: Tag or option to skip NewTCPTracker/NewUDPTracker (tunnel.go:479,615) and the per-second ticker, keeping only global atomics.
agent_opportunities.expected_benefit: Lower per-connection allocation and map contention on busy routers.
risks: RuleUpdate and close semantics rely on tracker Close in some code paths

agent_opportunities.name: Remove runtime geodata/UI/self-upgrade downloaders in Ultra profile
agent_opportunities.description: Tag out component/updater (UI zip, geo, core upgrade), sevenzip/zip, and pprof route.
agent_opportunities.expected_benefit: Smaller binary and fewer network-touching code paths on routers where packages are managed by opkg/apk.
risks: API compatibility with dashboards that call /upgrade

agent_opportunities.name: Default TUN stack choice per profile
agent_opportunities.description: Ultra/Lightweight keep mips (no gvisor) or system; Performance may enable with_gvisor+mixed. Possibly drop with_gvisor from router builds entirely (also drops tailscale).
agent_opportunities.expected_benefit: Avoids ~324 gvisor files and tailscale; kernel TCP via system stack for best throughput.
risks: mips/system stack behaviour on MIPS/ARMv7 untested here
Users selecting gvisor/mixed get error at config load

agent_opportunities.name: Cap relay buffer and pool retention for DIRECT splice path
agent_opportunities.description: Confirm copyDirect/splice triggers for DIRECT through the tracker/BufferedConn chain, and measure per-connection RAM/CPU with and without splice; consider a tag to force splice or smaller sing buf.BufferSize.
agent_opportunities.expected_benefit: Lower CPU per DIRECT byte and lower RSS per connection (hypothesis).
risks: Pipes use kernel memory (1 MiB F_SETPIPE_SZ) per active splice

agent_opportunities.name: Cap splice pipe size (e.g. 64-128 KiB) in low-memory profiles
agent_opportunities.description: Patch sing splice maxSpliceSize/F_SETPIPE_SZ via fork replace or vendored copy, tunable per profile.
agent_opportunities.expected_benefit: Hypothesis: lower kernel memory under many bulk flows; slightly more syscalls per MB.
risks: Needs measurement of syscall/CPU trade-off on target

agent_opportunities.name: Enable TUN GSO/GRO (tun.gso) when TUN is used
agent_opportunities.description: Turn on IFF_VNET_HDR offload and batch read/write in sing-tun with kernel 6.12; verify stack system/mixed.
agent_opportunities.expected_benefit: Hypothesis: fewer syscalls and per-packet stack traversals for TCP-heavy TUN traffic; main TUN throughput lever.
risks: driver/kernel quirks; sing-tun needs checksum handling bugs-free
does not help if TUN avoided in favour of redirect

agent_opportunities.name: Static Go cross builds per ARCH_PACKAGES
agent_opportunities.description: Ship per-arch static binaries: mipsel softfloat, mips softfloat, arm v7, arm64, amd64 with CGO_ENABLED=0.
agent_opportunities.expected_benefit: No libc dependency, simple packaging
risks: softfloat needed on MIPS or SIGILL
size limits on 16 MB flash devices

agent_opportunities.name: Keep binary on flash, avoid tmpfs copy
agent_opportunities.description: Install in /usr/bin, never copy to /tmp; document zram-swap as option on >=256 MB.
agent_opportunities.expected_benefit: Several MB RAM on small devices
risks: First-start latency from flash on slow NAND

agent_opportunities.name: Benchmark crypto on real MIPS/ARMv7 before any decision
agent_opportunities.description: Compare Go generic ChaCha20-Poly1305 vs Rust (RustCrypto soft, ring, aws-lc-rs) on an actual mipsel/ARMv7 router.
agent_opportunities.expected_benefit: Settles whether Rust crypto helps the main CPU cost.
risks: needs Tier 3 mips build via -Zbuild-std or OpenWrt buildroot

agent_opportunities.name: Use meow-rs / shadowsocks-rust as comparison baseline only
agent_opportunities.description: Run meow-rs on a real aarch64 router to get honest RAM/CPU numbers versus the tuned fork.
agent_opportunities.expected_benefit: Gives data point for the Go ceiling vs Rust ceiling.
risks: its published numbers are from a Mac

agent_opportunities.name: Optional sockmap offload module for long DIRECT TCP flows
agent_opportunities.description: After N KB of DIRECT traffic, switch the flow to sockhash redirect with an sk_skb verdict program; supervisor handles FIN/RST/timeouts.
agent_opportunities.expected_benefit: Removes remaining per-chunk wake-ups; gain over splice unknown (hypothesis).

agent_opportunities.name: Drop uber automaxprocs / set GOMAXPROCS explicitly
agent_opportunities.description: Remove automaxprocs (redundant with Go 1.25+ container-aware logic if go.mod go>=1.25, or pointless on bare routers) and set GOMAXPROCS from config.
agent_opportunities.expected_benefit: Small code/init reduction; deterministic CPU usage.

agent_opportunities.name: Pure-Go to assembly crypto swap for MIPS/ARMv7
agent_opportunities.description: Evaluate third-party assembly implementations (e.g. ChaCha20/Poly1305 for ARMv7 NEON) or cgo-free Go assembly; likely too costly to maintain.
agent_opportunities.expected_benefit: Several-fold on ChaCha20/Poly1305 on ARMv7 NEON (hypothesis).
risks: maintenance, security audit, FIPS-like module boundaries
MIPS has no SIMD target on most routers

agent_opportunities.name: PGO with a router-representative profile
agent_opportunities.description: Collect CPU profiles from a real router run (relay + DNS + rules) and commit default.pgo for release builds.
agent_opportunities.expected_benefit: 2-14% CPU per Go docs (generic), likely less here.
risks: build time and slight size growth

agent_opportunities.name: Trim init-time allocations
agent_opportunities.description: Lazily initialize large package-level tables (gopacket layer maps, pprof, regexp2 tables, protobuf registries) or drop the packages.
agent_opportunities.expected_benefit: Up to ~1.76 MB heap at startup saved at most (inittrace total), ~0.6 MB from the top few.

agent_opportunities.name: Process lookup compile-out for router builds
agent_opportunities.description: PROCESS-* rules are meaningless for LAN clients; add a tag making FindProcess a no-op and rejecting PROCESS-* rules at parse time.
agent_opportunities.expected_benefit: Removes /proc scans and netlink diag code; avoids accidental CPU burn from always mode.
risks: Configs from desktop profiles with PROCESS rules fail to load unless downgraded to warnings

agent_opportunities.name: UDP batching with recvmmsg/sendmmsg
agent_opportunities.description: Use ipv4/ipv6 PacketConn ReadBatch/WriteBatch in the generic UDP listener and DIRECT UDP socket.
agent_opportunities.expected_benefit: Hypothesis: fewer syscalls for high-pps UDP; negligible below ~20 kpps.

agent_opportunities.name: kTLS TX/RX for trojan/vless-tls
agent_opportunities.description: Port sing-box common/ktls to enable splice between plain socket and TLS socket.
agent_opportunities.expected_benefit: Hypothesis: small on CPUs without crypto offload; saves copies only.
risks: linkname hacks and build flags per Go version

agent_opportunities.name: io_uring / AF_XDP / MSG_ZEROCOPY
agent_opportunities.description: Not recommended.
agent_opportunities.expected_benefit: Negligible or unavailable on OpenWrt 6.12 default config.

agent_opportunities.name: Process-level control/data plane split
agent_opportunities.description: Separate helper process for relaying.
agent_opportunities.expected_benefit: None measurable over splice; duplicated Go runtime RAM.

agent_opportunities.name: Optional aarch64/x86_64 Rust helper for bulk workloads
agent_opportunities.description: A separate tiny Rust process (splice relay, DNS cache) enabled only on aarch64/x86_64 Performance profile, with Go fallback.
agent_opportunities.expected_benefit: Hypothesis: small RSS and CPU gain on aarch64 only; none on MIPS.

agent_opportunities.name: Replace gVisor TUN stack with Rust userspace stack
agent_opportunities.description: Only if TUN mode must stay in the Performance profile.
agent_opportunities.expected_benefit: Hypothesis: lower RAM than gVisor.

agent_opportunities.name: Xerj memory namespace for decisions
agent_opportunities.description: Store ADR summaries and measured numbers in a xerj memory namespace (e.g. mlw) for recall across sessions, mirroring DECISIONS.md/BENCHMARKS.md.
agent_opportunities.expected_benefit: Cross-session recall by meaning; complements Claude project memory.
risks: duplication with repo docs; repo docs remain the source of truth
